The Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh has received financing from the World Bank toward the cost of Technical Assistance Facility under the Learning Acceleration in Secondary Education (LAISE) Program and intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services.

The consulting services (“the Services”) include undertaking a comprehensive assessment of ICT infrastructure and institutional readiness, the status and readiness of Multimedia Classrooms (MMCs), and teachers’ competencies and readiness to deliver ICT-enabled teaching using ICT facilities and MMCs.

The detailed Terms of Reference (TOR) for the assignment can be found at the following website: www.dshe.gov.bd or can be obtained at the address given below. The duration of the assignment will be about 06 (Six) months. The assignment is expected to commence in March 2027.

Requirements/Salient Characteristics: The following specification lists the minimum requirements for a lock-in amplifier. Objective requirements are also highlighted when available. A lock-in amplifier is crucial for separating laser photodetector outputs from noise that may otherwise drown out the signal. Therefore, this lock-in component is necessary for meeting mission requirements. 3.1. The lock-in amplifier shall meet the following technical requirements: 3.1.1. Demodulation capability for DC up to 600 megahertz or higher reference signals 3.1.2. At least two analog BNC inputs 3.1.3. At least two analog BNC outputs 3.1.4. Analog to digital input conversion capability included, along with the inverse of digital to analog output conversion 3.1.5. Minimum sampling rate for input data of 1.25 giga-samples per second (GSa/s) 3.1.6. USB 2.0 or USB-C interface is supported 3.1.7. PC software interface included 3.1.8. Coding support for either Python or MATLAB languages 3.1.8.1. API for supported language must be given 3.1.9. Come with a manufacturer’s warranty of at least 1 year 3.1.10. Signal output must support digital to analog conversion of at least 1.25 giga-s
